fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01, I02, I05. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S02. Bradac p. 135 and Figs. 9.2-9.3; Neuroangio lateral atrial/direct lateral section.

fields.Course: Runs along the ventricular aspect of the caudate, with anterior and posterior longitudinal portions and transverse inputs.
fields.Tributaries: Transverse caudate and deep medullary veins.
fields.Outflow: Thalamostriate, direct lateral and posterior/inferior ventricular pathways.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Caudate head/body/tail and lateral ventricular contour.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Caudate head; caudate body; caudate tail; lateral ventricle Modelling interpretation Use the caudate and ventricular contours to form an interrupted arcade. Do not complete a circle solely to match a schematic.
fields.Variants: Anterior and posterior portions differ in dominance and continuity.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I02, I04. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S02. Bradac pp. 134-135; Neuroangio caudate veins section.

fields.Course: Pass approximately across the longitudinal collector from adjacent caudate/deep white matter territories.
fields.Tributaries: Caudate and nearby deep medullary venules.
fields.Outflow: Longitudinal caudate arcade and subependymal collectors.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Caudate arcade; ventricular wall Modelling interpretation Author a few short examples. Avoid a dense, uniformly spaced lattice.
fields.Naming: Separate these from the larger transverse medullary veins of the brainstem.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I04. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S02. Bradac pp. 134-135; Neuroangio caudate veins section.
fields.Alternate names: Inferior ventricular vein of the lateral ventricle

fields.Course: Runs anteriorly from the medial occipital/calcarine region into posterior callosal or adjacent Galenic tributaries.
fields.Tributaries: Medial occipital cortex and calcarine region.
fields.Outflow: Posterior pericallosal/Galenic system; basal connection possible.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Calcarine sulcus, medial occipital surface and quadrigeminal cistern.
fields.Bone and dura: Remote from the occipital bone; its course follows the medial occipital surface, not the inner table.
fields.Required landmarks: Calcarine sulcus; medial occipital surface; posterior Galenic region Modelling interpretation Approach the Galenic region from posterior/lateral cortex. Avoid duplicating the medial atrial vein.
fields.Naming: Internal occipital and anterior calcarine correspond in Bradac; retain source-specific naming.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I02. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S02. Bradac pp. 132-133; Neuroangio internal occipital example.

fields.Course: Emerges from the anterior thalamic region towards the anterior ICV near the foramen of Monro.
fields.Outflow: Anterior internal cerebral system; local tributary variation.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Anterior thalamus and ventricular floor adjacent to Monro.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Anterior thalamus; foramen of Monro; anterior ICV Modelling interpretation Add genuine thalamic tributaries separately from the larger caudate/thalamostriate arcade.
fields.Variants: Small tributary pattern and exact junction vary.
fields.Naming: Do not infer thalamic drainage solely from the name thalamostriate.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01, I02. General deep-system context; no dedicated normal anterior-thalamic example curated

fields.Course: Emerges inferiorly towards peduncular/basal or posterior mesencephalic collectors.
fields.Outflow: Peduncular, basal or posterior mesencephalic system.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Inferior thalamus and posterior perforated/interpeduncular region.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Inferior thalamus; posterior perforated substance; basal vein Modelling interpretation Keep these as tributaries rather than using a complete extra ring around the midbrain.
fields.Variants: Posterior components have alternative terminal routes.
fields.Naming: Additional group identified in Bradac during this catalogue review.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01, I03, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels

fields.Course: Transverse channels cross the hippocampal surface and join longitudinal collectors along the fimbrial/parahippocampal region.
fields.Tributaries: Hippocampus and neighbouring medial temporal tissue.
fields.Outflow: Inferior ventricular/basal system; posterior longitudinal connection to medial atrial drainage described in dissections.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Temporal horn floor, hippocampus, fimbria and parahippocampal surface.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Hippocampus; fimbria; temporal horn floor; basal vein Modelling interpretation Represent one longitudinal collector and a few transverse inputs. The whole family should not be drawn as a single inferior ventricular tube.
fields.Variants: Fine channels with source-dependent anterior/posterior subdivision.
fields.Naming: Transverse, anterior longitudinal and posterior longitudinal are components, not synonyms.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S15. Bradac p. 135; Rhoton Fig. 4.17 for posterior connection.

D15.name: Inferior striate veins                                         High | Representative network

fields.Course: Descends across insular sulci towards the insular pole, converging into the deep middle cerebral vein.
fields.Tributaries: Insular and adjacent deep opercular territory.
fields.Outflow: Deep middle cerebral vein; superficial Sylvian connections vary.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Insular surface, central and limiting sulci, limen insula.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Insular surface; limen insula; deep middle cerebral vein Modelling interpretation Add anterior, central and posterior representatives when the insula is registered. Keep them deep to the opercular surface.
fields.Variants: Posterior limiting-sulcus collector can be prominent.
fields.Naming: The insular tributaries are additional anatomy even though the deep middle cerebral trunk already exists.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01. Context and orientation; see source labels

fields.Course: Follows the temporal choroid plexus towards the basal drainage route, sometimes via the inferior ventricular collector.
fields.Outflow: Basal vein directly or via inferior ventricular vein.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Choroid plexus and choroidal fissure of temporal horn.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Temporal choroid plexus; choroidal fissure; inferior ventricular vein Modelling interpretation Attach to the plexus side of the fissure. Keep the plexus collector distinct from the broader ventricular-wall collector.
fields.Variants: Descriptions differ on direct basal versus intermediate inferior ventricular termination.
fields.Naming: Document the selected junction; do not silently equate it with inferior ventricular.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01, I06. Context and orientation; see source labels

fields.Course: Runs on the posterior orbital surface of the frontal lobe towards the anterior perforated/basal junction.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Orbital gyri and anterior perforated region.
fields.Bone and dura: Above the orbital roof, separated by brain coverings and CSF. This is cerebral drainage, not an orbital vein.
fields.Required landmarks: Orbital frontal surface; anterior perforated substance Modelling interpretation Use a small posterior orbitofrontal example, with its neural surface relation preserved.
fields.Variants: Anterior orbital frontal territory also has superior sagittal drainage.
fields.Naming: These terms can describe broader territories; qualify posterior basal drainage.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01. Context and orientation; see source labels

D21.name: Hypothalamic venous tributaries                                Detail | Reference first

fields.Course: Converges through deep white matter towards the ventricular subependymal network.
fields.Outflow: Caudate, septal, atrial and other subependymal collectors.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Centrum semiovale, corona radiata and ventricular walls.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: White matter; ventricular wall; receiving subependymal vein Modelling interpretation Use a few territory-specific examples with small calibre and tapered inputs. A DVA collector is not the normal template.
fields.Variants: Regional orientation, number and visibility vary.
fields.Naming: Medullary here refers to cerebral white matter, not the medulla oblongata.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I04. Context and orientation; see source labels

scope: Representative note-guided deep venous teaching reconstruction registered to existing brain surfaces; fine calibres and variable individual channels are illustrative.
